brief: Morgan Stanley argues AI investment is shifting from a technology story to a capital markets story. Its equity analysts expect combined capex for Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta to rise 57% in 2027 versus 2026, reflecting conviction that these investments can generate 25%+ ROIC. But 2027 free cash flow estimates for the same four hyperscalers keep moving lower because monetization lags capex deployment, widening the financing gap and reinforcing Morgan Stanley's view that AI-related credit issuance will stay substantial and may need to grow further. This summer, hyperscaler credit spreads widened as much as 35bp for higher-quality issuers and 50bp for lower-rated names before rallying sharply in the final two weeks. Widening was concentrated in higher-quality unsecured bonds, where issuance accelerated, while data center ABS and CMBS, backed by already-built, cash-flowing assets, saw more modest widening. AA-rated hyperscalers plus Nvidia and Broadcom are largely insensitive to funding-cost moves. Oracle (mid/low BBB) and data center developers such as former bitcoin miners and REITs have less balance-sheet flexibility, making funding costs a natural stabilizer of their future supply. The next phase shifts capex toward servers, chips and energy assets, favoring asset-level financing and a larger private-capital role.
